description: InterWeave's rules for runtime/github/arm.sh. boundary.paths is InterWeave CLAUDE.md's security-boundary list — identity and key handling, trust policy, wire or configuration parsing, persistence, admission and resource accounting, and anything cryptographic — in path form, matched case-insensitively. Whole trees where the tree is the boundary: the wire contracts and the normative configuration schema and examples (architecture/contracts/, architecture/config/ — a schema is the wire: #171 flipped one with no crate touched, and profile-config takes its ranges from config.schema.yaml); identity; every api/ contract crate; config parsing; discovery (peer-cache persistence, query budgets, untrusted peer and address input); the local IPC server and client; the transport stack; the human chat protocol, store, transport client and core (retention decides what content is durable); the two transport apps; the vendored third_party/ code; the normative vectors under fixtures/ (identity derivation, IPC framing — a fixture changes only with its contract); the root Cargo.toml, whose [patch.crates-io] points crates at third_party/ (the store caps ADR-0053 requires live there), so every root manifest change is reviewed (InterWeave #177 review, F1). Words where the boundary is a file anywhere: key, identity, seed, mnemonic, bip39, ed25519, secret, trust, crypt, sign, noise, tls, cipher, parse, codec, wire, protocol, persist, store, admission, quota, accounting, limit. Over-matching costs a review; under-matching costs a boundary. boundary.exempt is dropped first: Markdown and architecture/ prose outside the contracts and the config, tools/, xtask/, .github/, .claude/ and .agent-fabric/ — documentation and mechanical changes are not on the list. Cargo.lock and deny.toml are not on it: a dependency bump is mechanical until the owner rules otherwise. No classes: InterWeave arms under eight work commits only on the owner's word (CLAUDE.md §9). Declared by devex-tooling.
